What the labels mean

Before you submit: 8-point check

  1. Look it up here first. Confirm status and indexing, then confirm on the Scopus, Web of Science or DOAJ site.
  2. Verify the publisher. Real address, named editorial board, ISSN that resolves on issn.org.
  3. Check peer review. Reviews that take days or acceptance with no revisions are a warning sign.
  4. Read the fees. APCs must be stated up front. Hidden charges after acceptance are a red flag. Ask about waivers for Kenyan authors.
  5. Beware look-alike titles. Predatory outlets copy genuine journal names and logos.
  6. Check recent issues. Are articles real, on topic and regular? Gaps may mean inactive.
  7. Ignore unsolicited invitations. Flattering emails asking for papers are rarely legitimate.
  8. If in doubt, ask DRICE. Write to the Research Office before paying or submitting.
This registry combines the national accredited journal list (file of 11 Aug 2026) with DRICE tagging of 9 Oct 2026. Discontinued, inactive and unindexed journals are left out on purpose. Schools are assigned from journal titles, so a journal can sit in several schools or none. Fee status is verified only for journals marked Fee-free. Status is reviewed twice a year, and a listing is guidance, not a guarantee of recognition for promotion or grants.
